calls.reason: AI Incident Database lists agents acting on outside systems as its largest group but warns counts aren't frequencies. Anthropic says its internet-related cases had minimal real-world impact. Nothing measures the share caused by public agent deployment.

No matched comparison exists. But studies show agents with tools autonomously hacking real websites and, once hijacked, changing a user's account email. A text-only model can't take these actions, so agency plainly adds danger.
UK AISI found universal jailbreaks in every system it tested, but that covers a selected set of frontier models. No evidence covers the hundreds of models in his universal claim.

A secondary account confirms Axios reported many concerned employees. But its 'more than two dozen' counts sources familiar with debates, not alarmed employees, and the original article couldn't be read.

The June executive order rules out mandatory preclearance. But OpenAI has a board safety committee, and the attorneys general letter on Altman's conflicts raises allegations, not findings tied to release decisions.

Mixed: the International AI Safety Report says safety testing got harder, while AISI finds safeguards improving and OpenAI finds reasoning still easy to monitor. No longitudinal measure covers all three trends.
